In article <1998071415364800.LAA28509@ladder03.news.aol.com>,
  rossgetman@aol.com (RossGetman) wrote:

> In paragraph 30, TK is describing abolitionist John Brown or Alex's nature
> vigilantes.  He's not describing himself.

Hold on, a minute there, pardner!  One could (and I will) say that TK
*thought* he was describing these folks, but his own reasoning for violence
in pursuit of a cause as given in his journals (overcoming psychological
restraints) pegs him as psychologically very similar to the people he
describes in Par#30, over- socialized, true-believing leftist or not.

Again:

TK's Journal:
"As a result of indoctrination since childhood, I had strong
inhibitions against doing these things, and it was only at the cost
of great effort that I overcame the inhibitions.  I think that
perhaps I could now kill someone..."

ISAIF Par#30:
"By their own account, violence is for them a form of "liberation."
In other words, by committing violence they break through the
psychological restraints that have been trained into them. Because
they are oversocialized these restraints have been more confining
for them than for others; hence their need to break free of them."

I'd call TK's violence the "liberation" type.
Of course, a leftist and an anarchist can both use violence.

More:

"230. The more dangerous leftists, that is, those who are most power-hungry,
are often characterized by arrogance or by a dogmatic approach to ideology."

Anyone similar to himself, but with something other than the destruction of
technology in mind is a direct competitor since they are going to employ
technology (and valuable true-believers) in their battle.

I have no need for labels/categories on leftist vs. anything-else.  I just
think it's interesting that TK appears to be talking about himself.  I'm not
convinced otherwise.  You can give me all the TK leftist-related quotes in
the world... I just need a different angle.

> It's ironic that TK, in complaining about those who misrepresent him,
> is not complaining about his critics, but he's complaining about his
> supposed "fans."

How twu, how twu...

What is the status of this Sally Johnson report thing?
